input_files: eta/input.dat (temporarily set to the single-point kinematics above for the run, since exclurad hardcodes open(unit=5,file='input.dat'); restored to the original 10-point template afterward)
explanation: Ran ./eta/build/exclurad (model=3 EtaMAID/maid2000, rc_mode=0 full O(alpha) corrections, bmom=6.53 GeV, lepton=1 electron, ivec=1 recoil proton, vcut=0.166 GeV^2) for the single point W=1.5576 GeV, Q2=0.5552 GeV2, cos(theta*)=0.651724, phi*=72 deg. This is above the eta production threshold (W_thr = m_p+m_eta ~ 1.4862 GeV), so the kinematics are physical and the code converged (no NAG ifail error, no unphysical-point flag). Because exclurad.F opens unit 5 as the literal file 'input.dat' rather than reading stdin, the single-point input had to be written into eta/input.dat itself for the run (input_run.dat holds the same content for reference); the original 10-point template input.dat was restored afterward. Results were read from radtot.dat, which writes (per source line ~197-199): e1(unused,=0), W, Q2, cos(theta*), phi*, sigar(1)/sibar(1) [= delta, the ratio of radiated to Born unpolarized cross section, i.e. sigma_obs/sigma_0], sibar(1) [= sigma_born, the unpolarized Born cross section], plus radiated/Born beam-spin-asymmetry diagnostics (not requested here). Values are reported exactly as printed by EXCLURAD, unrounded. Units for sigma_born are EXCLURAD's internal 5-fold differential cross section units (gamma_v * sigma_0 from the code); the repository does not explicitly document the physical unit label (commonly nb/(GeV*sr^2) for this convention), so no unit conversion was applied or assumed.
